support: = 2.72×10 −3 m/s. 2 The direction of the acceleration is toward the center of the Earth. Discussion The centripetal acceleration of the Moon found in (b) differs by less than 1% from the acceleration due to Earth’s gravity found in (a). This agreement is approximate because the Moon’s orbit is slightly elliptical, and Earth is not stationary (rather the Earth-Moon system rotates about its center of mass, which is located some 1700 km below Earth’s surface). The clear implication is that Earth’s gravitational force causes the Moon to orbit Earth.

question: Which class of chemical messengers is released by an axon terminal to convey a nerve impulse to a neighboring neuron?
support: When a nerve impulse reaches the end of an axon, the axon releases chemicals called neurotransmitters .

question: Which model describes population growth when density-dependent factors slow growth as population size approaches the carrying capacity?
support: Under ideal conditions, populations can grow exponentially. The growth rate increases as the population gets larger. Most populations do not live under ideal conditions and grow logistically instead. Density-dependent factors slow population growth as population size nears the carrying capacity.

question: Approximately what proportion of all species that have ever lived on Earth does the support text state have gone extinct?
support: Extinction is the complete dying out of a species. Once a species goes extinct, it can never return. More than 99 percent of all the species that ever lived on Earth have gone extinct. Five mass extinctions have occurred in Earth’s history. They were caused by major geologic and climatic events. The fifth mass extinction wiped out the dinosaurs 65 million years ago.

question: Which term, defined as the ability to change or move matter and necessary for all life processes, describes the fundamental capacity organisms require to live?
support: Energy is the ability to change or move matter. All life processes require energy, so all living things need energy.

question: Which geologic principle explains why identical rock layers on opposite sides of the Grand Canyon are considered the same age because they were deposited at the same time?
support: Look at the Grand Canyon in Figure below . It’s a good example of lateral continuity. You can clearly see the same rock layers on opposite sides of the canyon. The matching rock layers were deposited at the same time, so they are the same age.

question: Which property of light, mentioned in the support text, makes it especially useful for astronomers studying distant stars?
correct_answer: It can travel across empty space
distractor1: It carries sound through empty space
distractor3: It is the only form of electromagnetic radiation
support: Earth is just a tiny speck in the universe. Our planet is surrounded by lots of space. Light travels across empty space. Astronomers can study light from stars to learn about the universe. Light is the visible part of the electromagnetic spectrum . Astronomers use the light that comes to us to gather information about the universe.

question: Which set of characteristics correctly describes oceanic crust according to the passage?
correct_answer: Basaltic composition; 5–12 kilometers thick; density ≈ 3.0 g/cm³
distractor1: Granite composition; >30 kilometers thick; density ≈ 2.7 g/cm³
distractor2: Basaltic composition; >50 kilometers thick; density ≈ 3.0 g/cm³
distractor3: Sedimentary composition; 5–12 kilometers thick; density ≈ 1.5 g/cm³
support: There are two kinds of crust. Oceanic crust is made of basalt lavas that flow onto the seafloor. It is relatively thin, between 5 to 12 kilometers thick (3 - 8 miles). The rocks of the oceanic crust are denser (3.0 g/cm 3 ) than the rocks that make up the continents. Thick layers of mud cover much of the ocean floor.

question: Which process described in the rock cycle returns an igneous rock to an igneous rock without first passing through sedimentary or metamorphic stages?
correct_answer: melting back to molten material and re-cooling into a new igneous rock
distractor1: breaking down into small pieces of sediment and becoming sedimentary rock
distractor2: being buried within the Earth and becoming metamorphic rock
distractor3: being uplifted and exposed to weathering and erosion
support: All rocks on Earth change, but these changes usually happen very slowly. Some changes happen below Earth’s surface. Some changes happen above ground. These changes are all part of the rock cycle. The rock cycle describes each of the main types of rocks, how they form and how they change. Figure below shows how the three main rock types are related to each other. The arrows within the circle show how one type of rock may change to rock of another type. For example, igneous rock may break down into small pieces of sediment and become sedimentary rock. Igneous rock may be buried within the Earth and become metamorphic rock. Igneous rock may also change back to molten material and re-cool into a new igneous rock.

question: Which of the following most accurately characterizes starch in plants?
correct_answer: A polymer of glucose monomers joined by covalent bonds that plants produce to store excess glucose
distractor1: A monosaccharide sugar used immediately by plant cells for energy
distractor2: A polymer of fructose monomers linked by ionic bonds used for structural support
distractor3: A type of protein synthesized by consumers that aids in digestion
support: Starches are complex carbohydrates. They are polymers of glucose. A polymer is a large molecule that consists of many smaller, repeating molecules, called monomers. The monomers are joined together by covalent bonds. Starches contain hundreds of glucose monomers. Plants make starches to store extra glucose. Consumers get starches by eating plants. Common sources of starches in the human diet are pictured in the Figure below . Our digestive system breaks down starches to sugar, which our cells use for energy.

question: Which explanation from the text best accounts for why technology has influenced diverse areas such as transportation, food production, manufacturing, communication, medicine, and the arts?
correct_answer: Technology has the goal of solving human problems.
distractor1: The primary aim of technology is to increase scientific knowledge.
distractor2: Technology exists mainly to preserve cultural traditions.
distractor3: The main purpose of technology is to generate profit for industry.
support: Important new technologies such as the wheel have had a big impact on human society. Major advances in technology have influenced every aspect of life, including transportation, food production, manufacturing, communication, medicine, and the arts. That’s because technology has the goal of solving human problems, so new technologies usually make life better. They may make work easier, for example, or make people healthier. Sometimes, however, new technologies affect people in negative ways. For example, using a new product or process might cause human health problems or pollute the environment.

question: In DNA sequence notation, what does a preceding lowercase 'd' (as in dGTAC) denote?
distractor1: That the sequence begins at the nucleotide with a free phosphate group (the 5′ end)
distractor2: That the sequence is written from the 3′ end toward the 5′ end
distractor3: That the DNA is double-stranded rather than single-stranded
support: Like proteins, nucleic acids have a primary structure that is defined as the sequence of their nucleotides. Unlike proteins, which have 20 different kinds of amino acids, there are only 4 different kinds of nucleotides in nucleic acids. For amino acid sequences in proteins, the convention is to write the amino acids in order starting with the Nterminal amino acid. In writing nucleotide sequences for nucleic acids, the convention is to write the nucleotides (usually using the one-letter abbreviations for the bases, shown in Figure 19.5 "Structure of a Segment of DNA") starting with the nucleotide having a free phosphate group, which is known as the 5′ end, and indicate the nucleotides in order. For DNA, a lowercase d is often written in front of the sequence to indicate that the monomers are deoxyribonucleotides. The final nucleotide has a free OH group on the 3′ carbon atom and is called the 3′ end. The sequence of nucleotides in the DNA segment shown in Figure 19.5 "Structure of a Segment of DNA" would be written 5′-dGdT-dA-dC-3′, which is often further abbreviated to dGTAC or just GTAC.

question: According to the text, what key anatomical characteristic defines a true coelom?
correct_answer: A fluid-filled body cavity completely enclosed by mesoderm that lies between the digestive cavity and body wall
distractor1: A partial body cavity filled with fluid that provides a hydrostatic skeleton (pseudocoelom)
distractor2: A fluid-filled cavity that is external and lined by epidermis
distractor3: A solid body cavity filled with connective tissue rather than fluid
support: Ancestors of roundworms also evolved a pseudocoelom. This is a partial body cavity that is filled with fluid. It allows room for internal organs to develop. The fluid also cushions the internal organs. The pressure of the fluid within the cavity provides stiffness. It gives the body internal support, forming a hydrostatic skeleton. It explains why roundworms are round and flatworms are flat. Later, a true coelom evolved. This is a fluid-filled body cavity, completely enclosed by mesoderm. It lies between the digestive cavity and body wall (see Figure below ). Invertebrates with a true coelom include mollusks and annelids.

question: Within the human gastrointestinal tract, which segment of the small intestine is the longest and is typically well over 10 feet long?
support: The digestive system is the body system that breaks down food and absorbs nutrients. It also gets rid of solid food waste. The digestive system is mainly one long tube from the mouth to the anus, known as the gastrointestinal tract (GI tract). The main organs of the digestive system include the esophagus, stomach and the intestine, and are pictured below ( Figure below ). The intestine is divided into the small and large intestine. The small intestine has three segments. The ileum is the longest segment of the small intestine, which is well over 10 feet long. The large intestine is about 5 feet long.

question: Which people are especially advised to adopt exercise, low-fat foods, and a healthy weight to reduce the risk of developing type 2 diabetes?
correct_answer: people who have family members with the disease
support: Type 1 diabetes and other autoimmune diseases cannot be prevented. But choosing a healthy lifestyle can help prevent type 2 diabetes. Getting plenty of exercise, avoiding high-fat foods, and staying at a healthy weight can reduce the risk of developing this type of diabetes. This is especially important for people who have family members with the disease.

question: Which remediation method involves injecting a reagent into an aquifer to chemically destroy contaminants in situ?
support: Chemical remediation can also treat water in the aquifer. A chemical is pumped into the aquifer. The chemical destroys the contaminant.

question: According to the passage, which human activity primarily contributes to the increased atmospheric carbon dioxide that leads to ocean acidification?
support: Ocean acidification occurs when excess carbon dioxide in the atmosphere causes the oceans to become acidic. Burning fossil fuels has led to an increase in carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. This carbon dioxide is then absorbed by the oceans, which lowers the pH of the water. Ocean acidification can kill corals and shellfish. It may also cause marine organisms to reproduce less, which could harm other organisms in the food chain. As a result, there also may be fewer marine organisms for humans to consume.

question: According to the passage, which property of cardiac muscle cells primarily enables the heart to contract as a unit and generate the force needed to push blood out?
distractor1: Each cardiac muscle cell contracts independently and asynchronously
distractor2: High elastic recoil of the cardiac muscle fibers
distractor3: Composition mainly of skeletal muscle that allows strong voluntary contractions
support: To move blood through the heart, the cardiac muscle needs to contract in an organized way. Blood first enters the atria ( Figure below ). When the atria contract, blood is pushed into the ventricles. After the ventricles fill with blood, they contract, and blood is pushed out of the heart. The heart is mainly composed of cardiac muscle. These muscle cells contract in unison, causing the heart itself to contract and generating enough force to push the blood out.

question: A very large protein must cross the plasma membrane into a cell. Which cellular transport mechanism will most likely carry this protein into the cell?
distractor2: Facilitated diffusion through a carrier protein
support: 5. Assume a molecule must cross the plasma membrane into a cell. The molecule is a very large protein. How will it be transported into the cell? Explain your answer.

question: According to the passage, which scientific disciplines' decades-long advances are explicitly credited as necessary for activities such as driving a car, sending a text message, or turning on a light?
support: Physical science explains much of what you observe and do in your daily life. In fact, you depend on physical science for almost everything that makes modern life possible. You couldn’t drive a car, text message, or send a tweet without decades of advances in chemistry and physics. You wouldn’t even be able to turn on a light. Figure below shows some other examples of common activities that depend on advances in physical science. You’ll learn the "hows" and "whys" about them as you read the rest of this book.

question: What is the chemical formula for the glucose molecule synthesized during photosynthesis, as stated in the passage?

This is the process in which plants and certain other organisms (see Figure below ) synthesize glucose (C 6 H 12 O 6 ). The process uses carbon dioxide and water and also produces oxygen. question: Which specific intermolecular force described in the passage is chiefly responsible for water's unusually strong cohesion and relatively high surface tension?
support: Water is truly an amazing substance. It can exist in all three states under normal pressures and temperatures. At room temperature, it is a tasteless, odorless, colorless liquid, although it exhibits a blue hue when present in large volumes. Approximately 70% of the Earth’s surface is covered in water. For a small molecule, water molecules are highly attracted to one another, due to particularly strong hydrogen bonds. This leads to a number of properties, such as a relatively high surface tension. Unlike most other substances, water expands when it freezes. Water is also able to absorb relatively large amounts of heat with only minimal changes in temperature. This can be seen on a small scale, such as the coolant in your car, or on a larger scale, such as the more moderate climates in coastal areas. The water in the oceans acts as a tremendous heat sink, which influences global weather patterns. The clouds that form above lakes and oceans originate from the evaporation of lake and ocean water. They are byproducts of water’s thermal regulating capacity. Additionally, water is not only found here on Earth; scientists have found evidence of water on a number of extraterrestrial planets. In this lesson, we are going to take a look at this unique and important substance.

question: By approximately what percentage does maternal respiratory minute volume increase during pregnancy?
support: 28.4 Maternal Changes During Pregnancy, Labor, and Birth Hormones (especially estrogens, progesterone, and hCG) secreted by the corpus luteum and later by the placenta are responsible for most of the changes experienced during pregnancy. Estrogen maintains the pregnancy, promotes fetal viability, and stimulates tissue growth in the mother and developing fetus. Progesterone prevents new ovarian follicles from developing and suppresses uterine contractility. Pregnancy weight gain primarily occurs in the breasts and abdominal region. Nausea, heartburn, and frequent urination are common during pregnancy. Maternal blood volume increases by 30 percent during pregnancy and respiratory minute volume increases by 50 percent. The skin may develop stretch marks and melanin production may increase.

question: Which type of weapon is designed to increase the fraction of energy released as radiation so it can irradiate advancing enemy troops while minimizing blast and thermal casualties to friendly forces?
support: The energy yield and the types of energy produced by nuclear bombs can be varied. Energy yields in current arsenals range from about 0.1 kT to 20 MT, although the Soviets once detonated a 67 MT device. Nuclear bombs differ from conventional explosives in more than size. Figure 32.34 shows the approximate fraction of energy output in various forms for conventional explosives and for two types of nuclear bombs. Nuclear bombs put a much larger fraction of their output into thermal energy than do conventional bombs, which tend to concentrate the energy in blast. Another difference is the immediate and residual radiation energy from nuclear weapons. This can be adjusted to put more energy into radiation (the so-called neutron bomb) so that the bomb can be used to irradiate advancing troops without killing friendly troops with blast and heat.

question: According to the passage, which property most reliably distinguishes the majority of elements such as iron (Fe) and copper (Cu) from the fewer nonmetal elements like hydrogen (H) and oxygen (O)?
correct_answer: They are shiny and good conductors of electricity and heat (metallic properties).
distractor1: They are primarily gases at room temperature.
distractor2: They commonly occur as pure elements in nature.
distractor3: They lack color and odor under standard conditions.
support: There are almost 120 known elements. As you can see from Figure below , the majority of elements are metals. Examples of metals are iron (Fe) and copper (Cu). Metals are shiny and good conductors of electricity and heat. Nonmetal elements are far fewer in number. They include hydrogen (H) and oxygen (O). They lack the properties of metals.

question: Which atmospheric process described in the passage causes water vapor to change into liquid droplets that form clouds?
support: The image below shows the role of the atmosphere in the water cycle ( Figure below ). Water vapor rises from Earth’s surface into the atmosphere. As it rises, it cools. The water vapor may then condense into water droplets and form clouds. If enough water droplets collect in clouds, they may come together to form droplets. The droplets will fall as rain. This how freshwater gets from the atmosphere back to Earth's surface.

question: Which structure formed during preprophase in plant cells is a sheet of cytoplasm that bisects the cell and suspends the nucleus at the cell center in preparation for prophase?
support: As plant cells have some structural differences compared to an animal cell, an additional stage prior to prophase is necessary. In plant cells only, prophase is preceded by a preprophase stage. Plant cells have a large central vacuole encompassing the center of the cell. Prior to the division of the nucleus, the nucleus must migrate to the center of the plant cell. To accomplish this, the cell forms a phragmosome , a sheet of cytoplasm that bisects the middle of the cell. The phragmosome suspends the cell nucleus in the center of the cell in preparation for prophase. Additionally, during this phase the plane of cell division is established. The accurate control of division planes, which establishes the placement of the future cell wall, is crucial for the correct structure of plant tissues and organs.

question: According to the passage, what characteristic is unique to birds among nonhuman vertebrates in terms of parental care?
correct_answer: Males as well as females incubate eggs and later care for the hatchlings (high level of male parental involvement)
distractor1: Only females incubate the eggs and provide care for the hatchlings
distractor2: Parents do not form pair bonds and abandon eggs shortly after laying
distractor3: Parents always remain together for life
support: After birds lay their eggs, they generally keep the eggs warm with their body heat while the embryos inside continue to develop. This is called incubation, or brooding . In most species, parents stay together for at least the length of the breeding season. In some species, they stay together for life. By staying together, the males as well as females can incubate the eggs and later care for the hatchlings . Birds are the only nonhuman vertebrates with this level of male parental involvement.

question: Which mass-wasting process involves the coherent downslope movement of large blocks of rock and soil along a curved surface, often leaving crescent-shaped scars and commonly triggered by a lubricating wet clay layer or by a river undercutting a slope?
support: Slump is the sudden movement of large blocks of rock and soil down a slope. You can see how it happens in Figure below . All the material moves together in big chunks. Slump may be caused by a layer of slippery, wet clay underneath the rock and soil on a hillside. Or it may occur when a river undercuts a slope. Slump leaves behind crescent-shaped scars on the hillside.

question: Which organ system is primarily responsible for exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide between the internal environment and the atmosphere?
support: organ system that brings oxygen into the body and releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

question: If a hummingbird's heart can beat up to 1,200 times per minute and this is described as "almost 20 times faster than the human resting heart rate," what approximate human resting heart rate does the text imply?
support: Birds have a relatively large, four-chambered heart. The heart beats rapidly to keep oxygenated blood flowing to muscles and other tissues. Hummingbirds have the fastest heart rate at up to 1,200 times per minute. That’s almost 20 times faster than the human resting heart rate!.

question: Which type of formula shows all the carbon and hydrogen atoms and the bonds attaching them, thereby identifying specific isomers by showing the order of attachment of the various atoms?
support: We use several kinds of formulas to describe organic compounds. A molecular formula shows only the kinds and numbers of atoms in a molecule. For example, the molecular formula C4H10 tells us there are 4 carbon atoms and 10 hydrogen atoms in a molecule, but it doesn’t distinguish between butane and isobutane. A structural formula shows all the carbon and hydrogen atoms and the bonds attaching them. Thus, structural formulas identify the specific isomers by showing the order of attachment of the various atoms. Unfortunately, structural formulas are difficult to type/write and take up a lot of space. Chemists often use condensed structural formulas to alleviate these problems. The condensed formulas show hydrogen atoms right next to the carbon atoms to which they are attached, as illustrated for butane:.

question: Which of the following is the correct set of unit symbols for the three commonly used temperature scales?
support: There are three temperature scales that are commonly used. Their units are °F (degrees Fahrenheit), °C (degrees Celsius), and K (Kelvin).

question: How does dormancy help many plants survive the winter after days grow shorter in the fall?
correct_answer: By suspending growth and development so they can endure extreme coldness and dryness
distractor1: By increasing metabolic activity to generate internal heat
distractor2: By producing seeds that immediately germinate during winter
distractor3: By shedding roots to reduce water uptake and loss
support: Many plants respond to the days growing shorter in the fall by going dormant. They suspend growth and development in order to survive the extreme coldness and dryness of winter. Part of this response causes the leaves of many trees to change color and then fall off (see Figure below ). Dormancy ensures that plants will grow and produce seeds only when conditions are favorable.

question: Which description best captures the properties of atoms given in the passage?
correct_answer: Smallest particles of matter that cannot be divided, created, or destroyed
distractor1: Divisible into smaller particles by chemical means
distractor3: Able to be created and destroyed under certain conditions
support: All substances are made of atoms. Atoms are the smallest particles of matter. They cannot be divided into smaller particles. They also cannot be created or destroyed.

question: According to the passage, which pair of roles do bacteria perform in the nitrogen cycle?
correct_answer: Converting nitrogen gas and decomposition products into nitrates that plants can assimilate, and returning nitrogen gas to the atmosphere
distractor1: Fixing atmospheric nitrogen directly into animal proteins and releasing oxygen
distractor2: Assimilating nitrates into animals and converting plant nitrogen back into nitrates
distractor3: Converting nitrates into ammonia for direct plant uptake
support: Bacteria play important roles in the nitrogen cycle. They change nitrogen gas and products of decomposition into nitrates, which plants can assimilate. Animals obtain nitrogen by eating plants or other organisms. Still other bacteria return nitrogen gas to the atmosphere.

question: According to the passage, why are hydrophobic molecules more likely to traverse the cell membrane's interior than hydrophilic molecules?
correct_answer: They preferentially interact with the membrane's hydrophobic interior (lipid tails).
distractor1: They readily form hydrogen bonds with water in the extracellular fluid.
distractor2: They are stabilized by forming ionic interactions with membrane phospholipids.
distractor3: They avoid interacting with other hydrophobic molecules.
support: Hydrophobic molecules “like” to be near other hydrophobic molecules. They “fear” being near hydrophilic molecules. The opposite is true of hydrophilic molecules. They “like” to be near other hydrophilic molecules. They “fear” being near hydrophobic molecules. These “likes” and “fears” explain why some molecules can pass through the cell membrane while others cannot.

question: Which organ is identified as the principal site for maturation of T lymphocytes in the passage?
support: Both types of lymphocytes are produced in the red bone marrow. They are named for the sites where they grow larger. The "B" in B cells stands for "bone." B cells grow larger in red bone marrow. The "T" in T cells stands for "thymus." T cells mature in the thymus gland.

question: Which representation provides the necessary information to derive the systematic name of a simple covalent compound?
support: The name of a simple covalent compound can be determined from its chemical formula.

question: Which combination of physical properties explains both why asteroids do not become round and why they cannot retain an atmosphere?
correct_answer: Their small size gives them insufficient gravity and they have no internal heat
distractor1: Their highly elliptical orbits and rapid rotation
distractor2: Their composition of ice and rock
distractor3: Their proximity to the Sun and high surface temperatures
support: Asteroids are very small, irregularly shaped, rocky bodies. Asteroids orbit the Sun, but they are more like giant rocks than planets. Since they are small, they do not have enough gravity to become round. They are too small to have an atmosphere. With no internal heat, they are not geologically active. An asteroid can only change due to a collision. A collision may cause the asteroid to break up. It may create craters on the asteroid’s surface. An asteroid may strike a planet if it comes near enough to be pulled in by its gravity. Figure below shows a typical asteroid.

question: The passage states that carbon dioxide can exist as a liquid only under which condition?
distractor2: at extremely low temperatures without added pressure
support: Solid carbon dioxide is called dry ice because it does not pass through the liquid phase. Instead, it does directly to the gas phase. (Carbon dioxide can exist as liquid but only under high pressure. ) Dry ice has many practical uses, including the long-term preservation of medical samples.

question: According to ecosystem function, which component is recycled through ecosystems rather than requiring a continual external supply?
support: Ecosystems need a constant input of energy for their organisms, but matter is recycled through ecosystems.

question: Under which condition is it possible to form compounds containing the Hg2 2+ ion?
correct_answer: When there is a large excess of mercury
support: Most mercury compounds decompose when heated. Most mercury compounds contain mercury with a 2+-oxidation state. When there is a large excess of mercury, it is possible to form compounds containing the Hg 2 2+ ion. All mercury compounds are toxic, and it is necessary to exercise great care in their synthesis.

question: According to the passage, why might a puppy that has a genetic tendency to interact normally with other dogs still fail to display those normal behaviors?
correct_answer: It was raised in isolation without exposure to other dogs
distractor1: Because its genes predispose it to fear rather than normal interaction
distractor2: Because normal behaviors are entirely learned and genes play no role
distractor3: Because exposure to humans during development prevents canine social behaviors
support: In reality, most animal behaviors are not controlled by nature or nurture. Instead, they are influenced by both nature and nurture. In dogs, for example, the tendency to behave toward other dogs in a certain way is probably controlled by genes. However, the normal behaviors can’t develop in an environment that lacks other dogs. A puppy raised in isolation from other dogs may never develop the normal behaviors. It may always fear other dogs or act aggressively toward them.

question: Which characteristic of the window screen is used as an analogy for the cell membrane's function?
correct_answer: It lets some things pass through while keeping other things out (selective permeability)
distractor1: It actively pumps substances in and out of the cell
distractor2: It serves as a rigid structural barrier like a cell wall
distractor3: It only allows liquids to pass, not gases or solids
support: This window screen has a fly on it. In a way, the window screen is like a cell membrane. It lets some things pass through while keeping other things out. Air molecules and raindrops can pass through the screen, but larger objects like the fly cannot. In the first lesson of this chapter, you'll learn about different ways that substances can pass through the cell membrane. You'll find out how the cell membrane lets some substances pass through while keeping other substances out.

question: What is the primary reason triploid animals are typically sterile?
correct_answer: Meiosis cannot proceed normally with an odd number of chromosome sets.
distractor1: Inactivation of extra X chromosomes causes lethal gene-dosage imbalance.
distractor2: Triploids lack sex chromosomes and therefore cannot form gametes.
distractor3: Polyploidy is universally lethal in animals, so triploids die before reproductive maturity.
support: In an individual carrying an abnormal number of X chromosomes, cellular mechanisms will inactivate all but one X in each of her cells. As a result, X-chromosomal abnormalities are typically associated with mild mental and physical defects, as well as sterility. If the X chromosome is absent altogether, the individual will not develop. Several errors in sex chromosome number have been characterized. Individuals with three X chromosomes, called triplo-X, appear female but express developmental delays and reduced fertility. The XXY chromosome complement, corresponding to one type of Klinefelter syndrome, corresponds to male individuals with small testes, enlarged breasts, and reduced body hair. The extra X chromosome undergoes inactivation to compensate for the excess genetic dosage. Turner syndrome, characterized as an X0 chromosome complement (i. , only a single sex chromosome), corresponds to a female individual with short stature, webbed skin in the neck region, hearing and cardiac impairments, and sterility. An individual with more than the correct number of chromosome sets (two for diploid species) is called polyploid. For instance, fertilization of an abnormal diploid egg with a normal haploid sperm would yield a triploid zygote. Polyploid animals are extremely rare, with only a few examples among the flatworms, crustaceans, amphibians, fish, and lizards. Triploid animals are sterile because meiosis cannot proceed normally with an odd number of chromosome sets. In contrast, polyploidy is very common in the plant kingdom, and polyploid plants tend to be larger and more robust than euploids of their species.

question: Which statement below is accurately supported by the passage about the distribution of Earth's water?
correct_answer: Only about 3 percent of Earth's water is fresh, and most of that freshwater is frozen in glaciers and polar ice caps.
distractor1: Most of Earth's freshwater is found in rivers and lakes.
distractor2: Icebergs commonly form only from chunks of ice that break off mountain glaciers.
distractor3: Nearly all of Earth's water is stored underground in spaces between rocks.
support: Most of Earth’s water is salt water in the oceans. As Figure below shows, only 3 percent of Earth’s water is fresh. Freshwater is water that contains little or no dissolved salt. Most freshwater is frozen in ice caps and glaciers. Glaciers cover the peaks of some tall mountains. For example, the Cascades Mountains in North America and the Alps Mountains in Europe are capped with ice. Ice caps cover vast areas of Antarctica and Greenland. Chunks of ice frequently break off ice caps. They form icebergs that float in the oceans.

question: Which equation did Hertz use to calculate the propagation speed of the electromagnetic waves after determining wavelength from interference patterns and knowing their frequency?
support: Hertz also studied the reflection, refraction, and interference patterns of the electromagnetic waves he generated, verifying their wave character. He was able to determine wavelength from the interference patterns, and knowing their frequency, he could calculate the propagation speed using the equation υ = fλ (velocity—or speed—equals frequency times wavelength). Hertz was thus able to prove that electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light. The SI unit for frequency, the hertz ( 1 Hz = 1 cycle/sec ), is named in his honor.

question: What molecular feature of erythrocytes determines ABO and Rhesus (Rh) blood groups and is critical for transfusion compatibility?
correct_answer: surface antigens on red blood cells
support: Specific antigens on the surface of red blood cells determine blood type. The best-known blood types are ABO and Rhesus (Rh) blood types. Blood type is important in cases of blood transfusion. A patient must receive blood of his or her own blood type to avoid clumping of red blood cells.

question: According to the passage, how are intrusive igneous rocks that formed below the surface most commonly brought into view?
correct_answer: Erosion of the rock and sediment that covers them
distractor3: Cooling and solidifying at the surface
support: Extrusive igneous rocks cool at the surface. Volcanoes are one type of feature that forms from extrusive rocks. Several other interesting landforms are also extrusive features. Intrusive igneous rocks cool below the surface. These rocks do not always remain hidden. Rocks that formed in the crust are exposed when the rock and sediment that covers them is eroded away.

question: Which molecular event most directly permits NF-κB to translocate into the nucleus and stimulate transcription?
correct_answer: Phosphorylation of the inhibitor IκB dissociates the complex between IκB and NF-κB, allowing NF-κB to enter the nucleus and activate transcription.
distractor1: A small, hydrophobic ligand binds directly to NF-κB, activating it.

question: Which statement correctly describes how the hypothalamus controls the anterior versus the posterior pituitary?
correct_answer: The anterior pituitary is regulated by hypothalamic releasing and release‑inhibiting hormones, whereas the posterior pituitary stores and releases hormones produced in the hypothalamus that are transported along axons/neurosecretory cells.
distractor1: The anterior pituitary stores and releases hormones produced in the hypothalamus via axonal transport, while the posterior pituitary is regulated by hypothalamic releasing and release‑inhibiting hormones.
distractor2: Both the anterior and posterior pituitary secrete hormones independently of the hypothalamus, receiving no regulatory signals from it.
distractor3: Both anterior and posterior pituitary hormones are delivered to the pituitary by axonal transport from hypothalamic neurons.
support: Hypothalamic-Pituitary Axis The hypothalamus in vertebrates integrates the endocrine and nervous systems. The hypothalamus is an endocrine organ located in the diencephalon of the brain. It receives input from the body and other brain areas and initiates endocrine responses to environmental changes. The hypothalamus acts as an endocrine organ, synthesizing hormones and transporting them along axons to the posterior pituitary gland. It synthesizes and secretes regulatory hormones that control the endocrine cells in the anterior pituitary gland. The hypothalamus contains autonomic centers that control endocrine cells in the adrenal medulla via neuronal control. The pituitary gland, sometimes called the hypophysis or “master gland” is located at the base of the brain in the sella turcica, a groove of the sphenoid bone of the skull, illustrated in Figure 37.15. It is attached to the hypothalamus via a stalk called the pituitary stalk (or infundibulum). The anterior portion of the pituitary gland is regulated by releasing or release-inhibiting hormones produced by the hypothalamus, and the posterior pituitary receives signals via neurosecretory cells to release hormones produced by the hypothalamus. The pituitary has two distinct regions—the anterior pituitary and the posterior pituitary—which between them secrete nine different peptide or protein hormones. The posterior lobe of the pituitary gland contains axons of the hypothalamic neurons.

question: In the magnesium rod–steel pipeline corrosion protection system, what role does the soil between the anode and cathode play?
correct_answer: It acts as the salt bridge that completes the electrical circuit and maintains electrical neutrality.
distractor1: It serves as the cathode where oxygen is reduced.
distractor2: It provides an oxide barrier that prevents further corrosion.
distractor3: It forces magnesium to act as the cathode by reversing the cell’s polarity.
support: Connecting a magnesium rod to an underground steel pipeline protects the pipeline from corrosion. Because magnesium (E° = −2.37 V) is much more easily oxidized than iron (E° = −0.45 V), the Mg rod acts as the anode in a galvanic cell. The pipeline is therefore forced to act as the cathode at which oxygen is reduced. The soil between the anode and the cathode acts as a salt bridge that completes the electrical circuit and maintains electrical neutrality. As Mg(s) is oxidized to Mg2+ at the anode, anions in the soil, such as nitrate, diffuse toward the anode to neutralize the positive charge. Simultaneously, cations in the soil, such as H+ or NH4+, diffuse toward the cathode, where they replenish the protons that are consumed as oxygen is reduced. A similar strategy uses many miles of somewhat less reactive zinc wire to protect the Alaska oil pipeline.

support: Adolescents may have mood swings because of surging hormones .

question: According to the support text, which pair of magnet poles will attract each other?
correct_answer: A north pole and a south pole of two magnets

distractor2: Two south poles of two magnets
distractor3: A north pole and a north pole of two magnets

question: According to the text, where are most blood cells produced?
support: The skeletal system makes blood cells. Most blood cells are produced inside certain types of bones.

question: What happens to sediment size as the slope of a stream or river becomes less steep?
distractor2: All sediment sizes are carried without dropping.
distractor3: Sediments stop being deposited regardless of slope.
support: When a stream or river slows down, it starts dropping its sediments. Larger sediments are dropped in steep areas, but smaller sediments can still be carried. Smaller sediments are dropped as the slope becomes less steep.

question: The passage states that combining the two equations from photosynthesis and cellular respiration demonstrates what?
correct_answer: how energy flows and how the carbon and oxygen cycle between organisms and the environment
distractor1: how nutrients are broken down during digestion
distractor2: how water moves through cell membranes by osmosis
distractor3: how genetic information is copied and transmitted during reproduction
support: Cellular respiration, in many ways the opposite of photosynthesis, shows the interdependence of producers and consumers. Combined, the two equations demonstrate how energy flows and the carbon and oxygen cycle between organisms and environment.

question: In mitochondria, what feature of the inner membrane increases the surface area for proteins and molecules involved in cellular respiration?
distractor1: A single outer membrane that directly faces the cytosol
distractor2: The fluid-filled matrix located inside the inner membrane
distractor3: Sequencing of enzyme and electron carrier molecules in the cytosol
support: Mitochondria, shown here as the green ovals in this animal cell, are membranous organelles which sequence enzyme and electron carrier molecules to make cellular respiration highly efficient. Mitochondria have both an inner and outer membrane, with a matrix inside the inner membrane. The inner membrane has many internal folds, increasing the surface area for proteins and molecules involved in cellular respiration.

question: In the formation of a solution, what is the substance that dissolves the solute called?
support: A solution forms when one substance dissolves in another. The substance that dissolves is called the solute. The substance that dissolves it is called the solvent.

question: According to the text, the earliest known fossil flowers were about how old?
support: Flowering plants are thought to have evolved at least 200 million years ago from gymnosperms like Gnetae. The earliest known fossils of flowering plants are about 125 million years old. The fossil flowers have male and female reproductive organs but no petals or sepals.

question: Retroviruses are RNA viruses that synthesize DNA in the host cell from their what?
support: mutation. The chemical and/or physical agents that cause mutations are called mutagens. Diseases that occur due to mutations in critical DNA sequences are referred to as genetic diseases. Viruses are infectious agents composed of a tightly packed central core of nucleic acids enclosed by a protective shell of proteins. Viruses contain either DNA or RNA as their genetic material but not both. Some RNA viruses, calledretroviruses, synthesize DNA in the host cell from their RNA genome. The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) causes acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).

question: According to the text, why does friction occur?
correct_answer: because no surface is perfectly smooth
distractor1: because the objects are always moving at the same speed
distractor2: because heavier objects float on the surface
distractor3: because surfaces attract each other without contact
support: Friction occurs because no surface is perfectly smooth.

question: According to the passage, what distinguishes the three types of muscle tissue from one another?
correct_answer: The different arrangements of their muscle fibers
distractor1: The type of tissue membrane surrounding the fibers
distractor2: The number of muscle types found in the nervous system
distractor3: The presence of three different kinds of nerves in the fibers
support: There are three different types of muscle tissue in the human body: cardiac, smooth, and skeletal muscle tissues. All three types consist mainly of muscle fibers, but the fibers have different arrangements. You can see how each type of muscle tissue looks in Figure below .

question: According to the text, the speed of a wave through connected harmonic oscillators depends on the distance between them, the spring constant, and the what?
support: Most wave media act like a series of connected oscillators. For instance, a rope can be thought of as a large number of masses (molecules) connected by springs (intermolecular forces). The speed of a wave through connected harmonic oscillators depends on the distance between them, the spring constant, and the mass. In this way, we can model wave media using the principles of simple harmonic motion.

question: Inheritance is more complex for traits with which type of dominance or pattern of allele expression?
support: Inheritance is more complex for traits in which there is codominance or incomplete dominance. Traits may also be controlled by multiple alleles or multiple genes. Many traits are influenced by the environment as well.

question: According to the passage, how many atoms does water contain?
support: Water is a simple molecule, containing just three atoms. Nonetheless, water’s structure gives it unique properties that help explain why it is vital to all living organisms.

question: Which statement best describes how different visible light wavelengths relate to perceived color?
correct_answer: Different wavelengths of visible light appear as different colors.
distractor1: Visible light consists of wavelengths that fall between infrared light and ultraviolet light.
distractor2: It is the only light that people can see.
distractor3: Visible light has a very wide range of wavelengths.
support: Visible light consists of a very narrow range of wavelengths that falls between infrared light and ultraviolet light. It is the only light that people can see. Different wavelengths of visible light appear as different colors.

question: On what basis is the Linnaean system said to be based, and what hierarchy does it use (from which to which taxon)?
correct_answer: Similarities in obvious physical traits; a hierarchy of taxa from kingdom to species.
distractor1: Genetic sequence differences; a hierarchy of taxa from species to kingdom.
distractor2: Environmental adaptations; a hierarchy of taxa from domain to phylum.
distractor3: Behavioral similarities; a hierarchy of taxa from class to order.
support: The Linnaean system is based on similarities in obvious physical traits. It consists of a hierarchy of taxa, from the kingdom to the species.

question: In the first level of chromosome compaction, what happens to the DNA?
correct_answer: Short stretches of the DNA double helix wrap around a core of eight histone proteins at regular intervals.
distractor1: Nucleosomes and linker DNA coil into a 30-nm chromatin fiber.
distractor2: Fibrous proteins pack chromatin so each chromosome occupies a non-overlapping nuclear area.
distractor3: DNA is condensed into compact chromosomes solely by coiling into a 2-nm diameter fiber.
support: In the first level of compaction, short stretches of the DNA double helix wrap around a core of eight histone proteins at regular intervals along the entire length of the chromosome. The DNA-histone complex is called chromatin.

question: In the example of sugar dissolving in water, what term describes the table sugar within the mixture?
support: Imagine you have a cup that has 100ml water, and you add 15g of table sugar to the water. The sugar dissolves and the mixture that is now in the cup is made up of a solute (the sugar) that is dissolved in the solvent (the water). The mixture of a solute in a solvent is called a solution .

question: In the support text, which mineral is described as being made only of silver atoms?
support: All minerals have a definite chemical makeup. A few minerals are made of only one kind of element. Silver is a mineral made only of silver atoms. Diamond and graphite are both made only of the element carbon.

question: In the atomic structure described, what property is defined as the number of protons in the nucleus (Z)?
support: The number of protons in the nucleus is called the atomic number (Z) and is the property that defines an atom’s elemental identity.

question: In the described action potential, repolarization is when the membrane voltage moves back toward the resting membrane potential of what value?
support: Repolarization... meaning that the membrane voltage moves back toward the -70 mV value of the resting membrane potential. Repolarization returns the membrane potential to the -70 mV value that indicates the resting potential.

question: Which organ system feature do mollusks have according to the support text?
distractor1: A stomach that stores food without digestion
distractor2: Gills that only serve respiratory functions and never relate to circulation
distractor3: Malpighian tubules that exclusively replace the need for excretory organs
support: Mollusks have a true coelom and complete digestive system. They also have circulatory and excretory systems. They have a heart that pumps blood, and organs that filter out wastes from the blood.

question: What is the main function of rRNA described in the text?
correct_answer: to decode genetic messages in mRNA into amino acids
distractor1: to assemble ribosomes in the nucleolus
distractor2: to export ribosomes from the nucleolus to the cytoplasm
distractor3: to build proteins directly in the cytoplasm
support: The nucleus of many cells also contains an organelle called a nucleolus , shown in Figure below . The nucleolus is mainly involved in the assembly of ribosomes. Ribosomes are organelles made of protein and ribosomal RNA (rRNA), and they build cellular proteins in the cytoplasm. The function of the rRNA is to provide a way of decoding the genetic messages within another type of RNA, called mRNA for messenger RNA, into amino acids. After being made in the nucleolus, ribosomes are exported to the cytoplasm where they direct protein synthesis.

question: According to the passage, what state of matter makes up most of the matter in the universe?
support: In fact, plasma makes up most of the matter in the universe.

question: Mammals that are viviparous are called what?
support: Most mammals are viviparous. Their young are born live. They are born either as relatively large, well-developed fetuses or as tiny, immature embryos. Mammals that are viviparous are called therian mammals . Only a few mammals lay eggs instead of giving birth to an infant or embryo.

question: In the statement, proteins are described as polymers of amino acids, which act as what?
support: Proteins are polymers of amino acids, which act as the monomers.

question: How is Concept Biology Advanced organized according to the support text?
correct_answer: As a set of 18 concepts, each centered around a specific category and made up of lessons.
distractor1: As a single continuous curriculum with more than 550 lessons all focused on one topic.
distractor2: As a collection of 10 chapters, where each chapter covers a different biology field without lessons.
distractor3: As an online course that focuses on chemistry first, followed by biology concepts.
support: Concept Biology Advanced presents biology as a set of 18 concepts, with each concept centered around a specific category, such as cell biology or plants. Each concept is comprised of a series of lessons, with each lesson focusing on one specific topic.

question: According to the support text, what feature do invertebrates (like snails) lack?
support: Snails are an example of invertebrates, animals without a backbone.

question: Why would the presence of fossilized eggs near Deinonychus fossils suggest that it was endothermic?
correct_answer: Brooding would require sustained internal heat to incubate the eggs, which is consistent with endothermy.
distractor1: Brooding only requires external sunlight, so it does not imply elevated internal metabolism.
distractor2: Clawed hands alone determine egg incubation temperature, so the eggs’ location is irrelevant to metabolism.
distractor3: Endothermy would prevent egg fossilization, so nearby eggs indicate it was ectothermic.
support: The location of fossilized eggs near Deinonychus fossils suggests that it may have brooded its eggs. This would mean that it was endothermic. (Can you explain why?)

question: Why is mitosis unnecessary in bacterial (prokaryotic) cell division?
correct_answer: Because there is no nucleus or multiple chromosomes.
distractor1: Because bacterial genomes are linear instead of circular.
distractor2: Because bacterial cells do not replicate their DNA before division.
distractor3: Because binary fission does not produce genetically identical daughter cells.
support: Mitosis is unnecessary because there is no nucleus or multiple chromosomes. This type of cell division is called binary fission.

question: Why did scientists previously classify fungi as members of the plant kingdom?
correct_answer: They were thought to share obvious similarities with plants, such as being immobile, having cell walls, and growing in soil.
distractor1: Because fungi were proven to be fully photosynthetic and produce oxygen like plants.
distractor2: Because fungi are mobile organisms that actively swim in water.
distractor3: Because fungi lack cell walls and do not grow in soil.

question: What causes an earthquake to happen?
correct_answer: when so much stress builds up in the rocks that the rocks break
distractor1: when rocks release energy stored only in the soil above them
distractor2: when seismic waves travel through only one type of material
distractor3: when an earthquake’s energy is transmitted by volcanic gases
support: An earthquake happens when so much stress builds up in the rocks that the rocks break.

question: According to the text, the chest cavity example in our bodies is described as a system that is at what condition, and how is it damped?
support: In our bodies, the chest cavity is a clear example of a system at resonance. The diaphragm and chest wall drive the oscillations of the chest cavity which result in the lungs inflating and deflating. The system is critically damped and the muscular diaphragm oscillates at the resonant value for the system, making it highly efficient.

question: What type of reproduction do prokaryotic cells use to produce genetically identical offspring?
support: Prokaryotic cells grow to a certain size. Then they divide by binary fission. This is a type of asexual reproduction. It produces genetically identical offspring. Genetic transfer increases genetic variation in prokaryotes.

question: In stage II of catabolism, what common end product do the different pathways for carbohydrates, triglycerides, and proteins produce from the stage I breakdown products?
support: As you will learn in Section 20.5 "Stage II of Carbohydrate Catabolism" through Section 20.7 "Stage II of Protein Catabolism", there are specific metabolic pathways—which are different for carbohydrates, triglycerides, and proteins—that break down the products of stage I of catabolism (monosaccharides, fatty acids, and amino acids) to produce a common end product, acetyl-coenzyme A (acetyl-CoA) in stage II of catabolism.

question: Which type of environment do echinoderms occupy, according to the text?
support: Echinodermata are exclusively marine organisms. To date, no freshwater or terrestrial echinoderms are known.

question: Which event is described as unique to prophase I compared with prophase in mitosis and meiosis II?
distractor1: Homologous chromosomes do not pair up in this way
distractor3: Centrioles begin moving to opposite poles
support: Prophase I: The nuclear envelope begins to break down, and the chromosomes condense. Centrioles start moving to opposite poles of the cell, and a spindle begins to form. Importantly, homologous chromosomes pair up, which is unique to prophase I. In prophase of mitosis and meiosis II, homologous chromosomes do not form pairs in this way. During prophase I, crossing-over occurs (see below).

question: During phase one (excitement) of the sexual response, what occurs as a result of vasodilation in erectile tissues in both men and women?
correct_answer: The nipples, clitoris, labia, and penis engorge with blood and become enlarged
distractor1: The uterus and vaginal muscles contract in waves
distractor2: Breathing and heart rate decrease while the inner two-thirds of the vaginal wall enlarges
distractor3: The processes of the previous phases reverse and return to normal during resolution
support: During phase one, called excitement, vasodilation leads to vasocongestion in erectile tissues in both men and women. The nipples, clitoris, labia, and penis engorge with blood and become enlarged.

question: What type of sensory capability do the net of nerves in cnidarians provide?
support: Cnidarians have a simple nervous system. It consists of a net of nerves that can sense touch.

question: According to the support text, electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed through space. What happens to the frequency when the wavelength of such a wave becomes shorter?
distractor3: It becomes proportional to wave amplitude.

question: According to the text, what feature resembles a liver and gives liverworts their name?
support: Liverworts get their name from the type with the flattened bodies, which can resemble a liver ( Figure below ).

question: According to the passage, what do scientists use to record the length and strength of each earthquake?
support: Scientists use seismographs to record the length and strength of each earthquake.

question: Approximately how many species have scientists identified as alive today?
support: Scientists have identified about 1.9 million species alive today. Most estimates range from 5 to 30 million species.

question: In mining terminology, what best describes a rock that contains important minerals?
support: An ore is a rock that contains important minerals.

question: Rocks with mostly lighter colored minerals are formed from magmas that are what in composition?
support: Magmas that produce lighter colored minerals are higher in silica. These create rocks such as granite and rhyolite. Darker colored minerals are found in rocks such as gabbro and basalt.

question: Heat transfer by radiation occurs when what is emitted or absorbed?
distractor3: thermal motion of atoms at absolute zero
support: Heat transfer by radiation occurs when microwaves, infrared radiation, visible light, or another form of electromagnetic radiation is emitted or absorbed.

question: A tumor of the pituitary gland that causes growth hormone hypersecretion during childhood leads to which condition?
support: For example, a tumor of the pituitary gland can cause hypersecretion of growth hormone. If this occurs in childhood, it results in very long arms and legs and abnormally tall stature by adulthood. The condition is commonly known as gigantism.

question: Which hormone is produced by the kidneys and stimulates the absorption of calcium and phosphate from the digestive tract?
support: Additionally, calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D, is produced by the kidneys and stimulates the absorption of calcium and phosphate from the digestive tract.

question: In the support text, how is formal charge defined in terms of electrons and bonding?
correct_answer: Formal charge = valence electrons of a neutral atom − lone pair electrons − (1/2) bonding electrons
distractor1: Formal charge = valence electrons of a neutral atom + lone pair electrons − bonding electrons
distractor2: Formal charge = nonbonding electrons − valence electrons of a neutral atom − (1/2) bonding electrons
distractor3: Formal charge = valence electrons of a neutral atom − bonding electrons − lone pair electrons
support: formal charge results when we take the number of valence electrons of a neutral atom, subtract the nonbonding electrons, and then subtract the number of bonds connected to that atom in the Lewis structure. Thus, we calculate formal charge as follows: formal charge = # valence shell electrons (free atom) − # lone pair electrons − 1/2 # bonding electrons

question: Which property must a rock layer have to be a good aquifer, according to the support text?
support: A rock layer must be porous and permeable to be a good aquifer. An impermeable layer makes up the bottom of an aquifer.

question: In phylogenetic trees, a shared derived character is defined as a trait that is what?
correct_answer: derived at some point but not shared by all ancestors in the tree
distractor1: found in the common ancestor of the entire clade, shared by all members
distractor2: a trait that arises only after multiple new branch points have formed
distractor3: a characteristic that is identical across all organisms in the diagram regardless of clade
support: If a characteristic is found in the ancestor of a group, it is considered a shared ancestral character because all of the organisms in the taxon or clade have that trait... Only some of the organisms in Figure 20.10 have this trait, and to those that do, it is called a shared derived character because this trait derived at some point but does not include all of the ancestors in the tree.

question: In the described transmission cycle of Lyme disease, what organism first acquires the bacteria under normal conditions?
correct_answer: A tick bites a mouse and picks up the bacteria.
distractor1: A mosquito bites a human and picks up the bacteria.
distractor2: A human invades the natural habitat and picks up the bacteria directly from ticks.
distractor3: A tick bites a human and picks up the bacteria from the human bloodstream.

question: Which term describes the movement of the mandible away from the midline toward either the right or left side?
support: Excursion Excursion is the side to side movement of the mandible. Lateral excursion moves the mandible away from the midline, toward either the right or left side. Medial excursion returns the mandible to its resting position at the midline.

question: An end moraine is best described as a low ridge of sediments deposited at the end of the glacier that marks the greatest distance the glacier ________.
support: A moraine is sediment deposited by a glacier. A ground moraine is a thick layer of sediments left behind by a retreating glacier. An end moraine is a low ridge of sediments deposited at the end of the glacier. It marks the greatest distance the glacier advanced.

question: The proximal portion of which embryonic structure matures into the trachea?
support: At about this same time, an protrusion of endodermal tissue extends anteriorly from the foregut, producing a lung bud, which continues to elongate until it forms the laryngotracheal bud. The proximal portion of this structure will mature into the trachea, whereas the bulbous end will branch to form two bronchial buds.

question: According to the passage, what advantage comes from epiphytes being elevated high above the forest floor?
correct_answer: It can reduce the risk of being eaten by herbivores.
distractor1: It helps them obtain moisture from the soil.
distractor2: It guarantees that they will grow faster than plants on the ground.
distractor3: It prevents them from receiving air and sunlight.
support: Being elevated may also reduce the risk of being eaten by herbivores.

question: For an object undergoing simple harmonic motion on a frictionless surface attached to a spring, when displaced from equilibrium, when does it reach its maximum speed?
distractor1: At the maximum displacement from equilibrium
